# Isleta 1.1.0
Isleta introduces itself on first launch, notifications open the island and show what they say, and the island stays at the notch through every kind of space switch.
## New
- **A setup guide the first time you open Isleta.** Four screens: what the notch is about to start doing, the one permission Isleta ever asks for, launch at login, and where to find the island. Leave it at any point — it does not come back. In the status menu as **Open Setup Guide**. - **Notifications open the island** and show the whole message — who it is from and what it says, not the first two lines. It closes itself a few seconds later, unless you opened the island yourself, in which case it stays yours. - **Swipe up with two fingers to close an open island.** Up is up, whichever way you have "natural scrolling" set. Swiping sideways still stows the island's content. - **Export Logs…** in the status menu writes a single file, wherever you choose, with everything needed to look into a problem. It offers to show you the file afterwards. - **Isleta keeps a log** at `~/Library/Logs/Isleta` — events only, never track titles or notification text, so the export is safe to send to a stranger. It never grows past a few megabytes. For more detail: `defaults write com.tryisleta.isleta VerboseLogging -bool YES`.
## Improved
- **The island opens to the size of what it is holding.** A wake greeting opens short, a notification opens as far as its message needs, and the player is unchanged. - **A notification no longer clips the app's name** into a 40-point sliver where "Messages" did not fit. VoiceOver still reads it out. - **Settings is five pages, not seven.** Shortcut is now a card in General. System held one switch that could never be turned on and is gone — what it explained is under Sources, beside the thing it is about. - **Sources reads as one list**, instead of four headings each repeated by the switch beneath it. - **Island opacity appears only if you have a display without a notch**, which is the only place it has ever done anything. - **Copy Diagnostics has left the status menu.** Export Logs… carries the same report and the history behind it.
## Fixed
- **The island stays at the notch when you switch spaces** — desktops, fullscreen apps, trackpad swipes and ⌃← / ⌃→ alike. No wait, no bounce, no blip, and Input Monitoring is no longer involved. - **Now Playing said the same sentence twice** in Settings — once as its description, once as its status. - **The settings sidebar drew page names through the Isleta icon** and the version number when you scrolled it.
## Requirements
macOS 26 or later, on Apple Silicon. Displays with a real notch get the island; a Mac with none gets a synthesized island on the primary display.
## Known limitations
- **Brightness has no HUD.** macOS offers no public way to read display brightness on Apple Silicon. - **Apple's own HUDs are not replaced.** Isleta shows its own alongside them; the switch that suggested otherwise is gone. - **The island sits above Mission Control.** In a real notch it covers nothing; a synthesized island can cover the centre of the space labels. - **A burst of notifications opens the island once for each.** Grouping them is a later release's job. - **The hover target is the notch itself** — 185×32 points, and easy to overshoot. - **Playing music costs about 0.4% CPU**, against an internal 0.3% budget. Everything else is inside budget. - **Not on the Mac App Store.** Signed with a Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and updated through Sparkle.

# Isleta 1.0.1
A maintenance release. The island now gets out of the way when you move between desktops and fullscreen apps, and the Welcome Back moment opens by itself.
## Fixed
**Launch at login works.** In 1.0.0 the switch was greyed out with "this copy of Isleta is not code signed" under it, on a copy that was signed and notarized. macOS reports a login item it has never seen before and one it cannot register in ways that are easy to confuse, and Isleta believed the wrong one — so the switch was dead for anyone who had not already turned it on, which is everyone. It is live now, and if the system does refuse, it says why instead of deciding in advance.
**The island no longer travels with a switching workspace.** Moving between spaces left it painted into the slide — pinned over two desktops sailing past, or welded to the arriving fullscreen app and drifting away from the notch, before snapping back to where it had been all along. It now goes off screen the instant a switch begins and arrives back at the notch with its usual bounce.
The cause is that a space transition photographs the screen rather than compositing it live, so the island had to be gone before the picture was taken — a few milliseconds after the switch starts, and well before anything can be redrawn. Every transition behaves differently: a desktop slide announces itself one way, entering a fullscreen app another, and leaving one a third, with nothing at all marking the end. Isleta now hides on anything that might be a switch and comes back once the system stops reporting, which is the only account of "finished" that holds for all of them.
**Settings opens in front, and in the middle.** The window used to arrive behind whatever app you were using — drawn correctly, but without focus, so the switches worked while the window looked dead and Escape went somewhere else. On a Mac that had never opened it, it also came up flush against the left edge and low instead of centred. Both are fixed, and a window you have moved yourself still opens where you left it.
**Quitting no longer strands a helper process.** Isleta reads Now Playing through a small `perl` helper, and an ordinary Quit was ending the app while the helper was still being told to stop — one orphan per launch, quietly accumulating until a restart. Teardown now waits for it, and any strays left behind by an earlier crash are cleared at the next launch.
**The status menu no longer shows a ⌘, next to "Open Isleta Settings".** Isleta has no menu bar to dispatch it from, so the shortcut it advertised opened the settings of whichever app was frontmost. Clicking the item does what it always did.
## Improved
**Welcome Back opens on its own.** The greeting used to wait behind a click. It now presents itself when you come back to the Mac, with a second line under the greeting drawn from a set written for the hour — morning, afternoon, evening and night each have their own, and the night ones know what time it is.
**The app icon's ripples are lighter**, which keeps them from over-brightening in dark mode.
## Requirements
Unchanged from 1.0.0: macOS 26 or later, Apple Silicon, and a display with a real notch — or a synthesized island on the primary display for a Mac that has none.
## Notes and limitations
Everything listed under 1.0.0 still applies. One addition worth knowing:
- **The island takes a moment to return after a space switch** — about a third of a second once the system has confirmed the switch finished. macOS provides no signal for the end of a space transition, so Isleta waits for the reports to stop rather than guessing; coming back sooner means reappearing in the middle of the animation.

# Isleta 1.0.0
The first release. Isleta turns the MacBook notch into an interactive surface — the Dynamic Island, done properly for the Mac.
At rest it is invisible: pure black filling exactly the cutout, its bottom corners following the cutout's own. Move the pointer onto the notch and it swells a few points on all three free edges while the trackpad taps once. Click and it opens.
## What's in it
**Now Playing.** Album artwork, a live equaliser, play/pause, skip, shuffle and repeat, and a scrubber you can drag to seek. Reads whatever is playing through the system's own media service, with an AppleScript fallback for Music and Spotify that listens for track changes rather than polling for them.
**Volume and mute.** The system HUD's information, in the notch, without a grey square in the middle of your screen.
**Notifications.** Incoming banners appear in the island. Requires Accessibility permission; Isleta is fully usable without it.
**Welcome Back.** A moment on wake and unlock, timed to arrive after the login shield has finished dissolving rather than during it.
**The shelf.** Drag files onto the island and it holds them, then drag them back out wherever you need them.
**Swipe and stow.** Swipe across the island to move between queued activities, or flick it left or right to stow it out of the way. Click to bring it back.
**Settings.** Hover delay, peek amount, activity dwell and synthesized-island opacity are continuous, each with something live reading it. Per-source switches, a global toggle shortcut that prints itself in *your* keyboard layout rather than assuming QWERTY, launch at login, and automatic update checks.
## Requirements
- macOS 26 or later, Apple Silicon. - Isleta presents only on displays with a real notch. An external monitor has no cutout for the island to be continuous with, so it gets none. A Mac with no notched display at all — mini, Studio, iMac — gets a synthesized island on the primary display instead.
## Notes and limitations
- **Brightness has no HUD.** There is no public route to observe brightness on Apple Silicon, so volume and mute ship and brightness does not. - **Apple's own HUDs are not suppressed.** The switch exists, off by default and reversible, but Isleta ships alongside the system HUD rather than in place of it. - **The hover target is the notch**, which is 185×32pt and easy to overshoot — especially with another display arranged directly above the laptop, where the pointer travels straight through. Discovery is an open design question, not a solved one. - **Playing music costs about 0.4% CPU** against an internal 0.3% idle budget. Everything else — cold launch, memory, idle with nothing on stage — is inside budget. - Not on the Mac App Store: Accessibility and the bundled media helper are incompatible with the sandbox. Isleta is signed with a Developer ID, notarized by Apple, and updates itself through Sparkle.
## Credits
Uses [Sparkle](https://sparkle-project.org) and [mediaremote-adapter](https://github.com/ungive/mediaremote-adapter), both BSD-3-Clause. Full acknowledgements are in the app's About pane.
